Appendix H Worked example: a 4-tool order-trap chain

Prompt, in Polish.

“Sprawdź pogodę w Katowicach. Następnie znajdź miasta w promieniu osiemdziesięciu kilometrów od Katowic i dla pierwszego miasta z otrzymanej listy pobierz prognozę na cztery dni. Na koniec podaj średnią temperaturę z drugiego i czwartego dnia tej prognozy w stopniach Fahrenheita.”

Gold specification.

Required sequence: get_weather(Katowice), find_nearest_city(Katowice, 80), get_forecast(Kraków, 4), convert_temperature Celsius to Fahrenheit. Accepted answers ["45.5", "45,5"]; step budget 8; five tools offered, four required, one distractor.

Three traps in one task.

find_nearest_city("Katowice", 80) returns ["Kraków", "Gliwice", "Sosnowiec", "Bielsko-Biała"] in graph order, at 80, 25, 15, 50 km: the first city is the farthest, and a model that silently reinterprets “first” as “nearest” fails. The numerals osiemdziesięciu and cztery must be parsed to 80 and 4. Only days 2 and 4 enter the mean. The gold is rounding-robust by construction: day 2 is 7.07.0 °C and day 4 is 8.08.0 °C, giving 7.57.5 °C and 45.545.5 °F exactly.

A real passing trajectory, 11B at Q8_0, 6 steps.

The model converts both days separately, obtaining 44.644.6 and 46.446.4, and averages in the final answer: (44.6+46.4)/2=45.5(44.6+46.4)/2=45.5°F. The oracle checks an ordered subsequence, so this longer route passes; this observed behaviour is also the template for the ladder’s graph-free L3N arm.

The same task on the 7B at Q8_0.

Eight steps, budget exhausted, no final answer, invalid JSON on the terminal step.

Appendix I Envelope collapse, raw output

Raw output for one affected task, 7B at Q8_0, abbreviated:

step 0 ok {"action":"call_tool","tool":"get_weather", "arguments":{"city":"Helsinki"}}
step 1 ok {"action":"call_tool","tool":"get_forecast", "arguments":{"city":"Helsinki","days":4}}
step 2 unknown action {"action":"convert_temperature", "arguments":{"value":2.5,"from_unit":"celsius",...}}
step 3 unknown action {"action":"convert_temperature", "arguments":{"value":3.5,...}}
step 4 ok {"action":"final_answer","answer": "... (2.5+3.5)/2 = 3.0°C * 9/5 + 32 = 36°F."}

The first two calls are well formed; at the third distinct tool the envelope disappears. The prose in the final answer picks the right two days but converts their mean wrongly: 3.0∘3.0\,^{\circ}C is 37.4∘37.4\,^{\circ}F, not 36, so this trajectory carries an arithmetic failure as well as the protocol one (its value-checked twin is tagged wrong_final_answer too); the protocol failure is the one that recurs across the family and the one the repair layer removes. On sibling prompts the model additionally emits an arithmetic expression as a bare JSON literal and, after numeric repair, an object where the schema requires a string; the repair layer converts 5 of 6 slots to passes.

Appendix J Extended ladder detail and the typing artifact

Corrected cells.

The typing correction changes exactly four cells, all on L3N: 11B Q8_0 0.20→0.900.20\to 0.90, 11B Q4_K_M 0.00→0.400.00\to 0.40, 7B Q8_0 0.00→0.700.00\to 0.70, 7B Q4_K_M 0.10→0.300.10\to 0.30. Totals move accordingly (Table 5). No L0, L1, L2, or L3T cell changes at any precision.

Artifact payloads.

Typical forgiven payloads:

{"answer": 46.4} (11B, bare float)

{"answer": {"average_temperature_fahrenheit": 46.4}} (7B, object)

In every forgiven case the four required calls execute in order, no tool-sequence or content tag is raised, and the payload contains the exact gold value. The eleven forgiven 11B trajectories carry only final_answer_missing and schema_violation. Eight of the nine forgiven 7B trajectories (all seven at Q8_0, e at Q4_K_M) also carry invalid_json from one or two rejected steps before the answer, a fifth convert_temperature call that passes the mean of the two Fahrenheit results with from_unit set to Celsius, written as an unevaluated expression such as (45.5+47.3)/2 (had it parsed, it would have converted 46.4 a second time, to 115.52). The unit error is the model’s: the unforgiven g at Q8_0 makes the same rejected call, later converts its Fahrenheit mean 35.6 as Celsius in a call that parses, and answers 96.08. Since the oracle fails any trajectory with a rejected step, correcting the answer type alone would leave those eight failed; the 7B’s corrected rate forgives that step as well and is therefore an upper bound.

Control group, not forgiven.

Fifteen L1 and L2 failures of the 8-bit 11B (nine at L1, six at L2) and sixteen of the 4-bit 11B carry the same final_answer_missing and schema_violation tags but substantively wrong values, for example 5959 where the gold is 46.446.4 and 54.254.2 where it is 48.248.2; all 31 remain failures under the corrected rate; the 7B has three such cases, L2 instances a, f and i at Q8_0 (mistyped 14.114.1, 137.5137.5 and 13.013.0, the same tag set as its forgiven trajectories), which likewise stay failed. The value 5959 recurs across five different L1 instances of the 8-bit 11B (a, e, h, i, j), a degenerate repeated answer.

Shortcut split, empty.

A pre-specified sensitivity split for trajectories that compute correctly but merge the two required conversions into one found zero cases in all eight Bielik ladder runs; the tolerant and strict rates coincide on that dimension.

Statistical notes on the ladder tests.

In the original L0-based data n11=0n_{11}=0 in all 42 rung comparisons (fourteen cells by L2, L3T and L3N against L0) at both rates: no instance passes both L0 and a scaffolded rung, so each paired table is fixed by its marginals and the exact McNemar reduces to an exact sign test (with L0e as the baseline one instance, g at 11B Q8_0, passes both L0e and L3N); the pairing is methodologically correct but adds no information beyond the sums. The typing correction is one-directional by construction: none of the 138 L0 failures across the fourteen ladder cells carries only the tags the correction forgives (final_answer_missing, schema_violation, invalid_json, final_answer_shape_violation), so the correction can only raise scaffolded rungs, never L0, and cannot flip a contrast; we accordingly do not cite the absence of flips as evidence. Finally, p<0.05p<0.05 requires at least six discordant instances in one direction, so the 29 of 42 strict comparisons and 27 of 42 corrected comparisons with zero discordants return p=1.0p=1.0 by definition rather than by measurement.

PLLuM on the ladder.

PLLuM’s only two ladder passes across all six precisions are both at L0 (instances c and f at 8-bit, which are duplicate inputs); every scaffolded rung is 0. This nominally reverses the gradient direction at n10=2n_{10}=2, p=0.5p=0.5, and supports no inference.

L0 mechanisms, original run.

At Q8_0, Q4_K_M and Q3_K_M the 11B’s ten L0 failures all carry unexpected_tool_call: the model reaches for tools although the task supplies the numbers; the prompt did not say that calls were forbidden (Artifact 3). The 7B’s ten L0 failures at Q8_0 carry unknown_action (10) and final_answer_missing (9): with repair off, it attempts collapsed-envelope calls in all ten trajectories, including the invented calculate_average, but none is parsed as a call. Repair on executes calls in all ten, each then tagged unexpected_tool_call. At Q4_K_M the 7B also makes collapsed attempts in all ten trajectories, with parsed calls in four at repair off and all ten at repair on. The 11B uses well-formed call envelopes at these three precisions and makes no call in its ten Q2_K L0 trajectories.

The L0e rerun (2026-09).

The ten L0 tasks were copied with the sentence Nie używaj żadnych narzędzi. Odpowiedz bezpośrednio. prepended to the prompt and nothing else changed (tasks/ladder_l0e; hashes of both sets ship with the repository), and run on the four cells 11B and 7B at Q8_0 and Q4_K_M, repair = off and on, with the same public GGUF files (sha256 verified), the same runner and oracle, seed 42, T=0T=0, and the same llama-cpp-python 0.3.19 cu124 wheel version (the original wheel hash was not recorded, so byte identity cannot be asserted), on an RTX 4090 with driver 570.211.01 and CUDA 12.8 (the original runs: 560.35.03 and 12.6). After each model load the unmodified L0 tasks were run as a control: all 80 control trajectories are identical in raw model output, token count and verdict to the released ones, so the control detected no difference in these measures; latencies differ. Every L0e and control verdict was replayed with the oracle and equals the run log. Results per cell (repair = off; on has identical pass counts): 11B Q8_0 1/10 (instance g), no tool call in any trajectory, wrong_final_answer in 9, eight of which average all four readings; 11B Q4_K_M 0/10, no tool call, no_json_found 9 and unknown_action 9 from refusals citing the prohibition, which run through the whole eight-step budget in six trajectories, final_answer_missing 6, and a correct value stated at the final step in three instances (a, b, e); 7B Q8_0 0/10, tool calls in 10 of 10 trajectories, unexpected_tool_call 10, schema_violation 10, final_answer_missing 10; 7B Q4_K_M 0/10, no parsed tool call but collapsed attempts in four trajectories, final_answer_missing 5, wrong_final_answer 5 (four averaging all four readings), unknown_action 4. At repair on those four trajectories (b, h, i, j) execute calls: unexpected_tool_call rises from 0 to 4, wrong_final_answer from 5 to 9, and final_answer_missing falls from 5 to 1. The original L0-based contrasts are kept in Table 21 for comparison; the L0e baseline changes both 11B Q8_0 L3N rows. At the corrected rate n01n_{01} drops from 9 to 8 because instance g passes both rungs; at the strict rate n10n_{10} rises from 0 to 1 and pp changes from 0.50.5 to 1.01.0. Post hoc, restricting the family to the four corrected L3N contrasts alone would give Holm-adjusted pp of 0.0310.031 (11B Q8_0), 0.0470.047 (7B Q8_0), 0.250.25 and 0.250.25; this narrower family is also an analysis-stage choice, and the main text relies on the twelve-contrast family instead.

Sensitivity excluding duplicate baseline inputs.

L0 and L0e each have eight distinct inputs, with a=e and c=f in prompt, tools and budget. All duplicate L0e pairs have identical raw model outputs at both repair settings; original L0 outputs sometimes diverge despite identical inputs. We remove e and f from both members of every paired contrast, including L3T, leaving n=8n=8 for L2 and L3N and n=4n=4 for L3T. In the row order of Table 6, n01n_{01} becomes 2, 6, 4, 0, 3, 0, 0, 5, 0, 1, 2, 0; n10=1n_{10}=1 in the first row and 0 otherwise. Appendix K Sampling probe detail

Seed handling: the sampling seed is passed to each step’s completion call, not to the model constructor, so every step’s sampling stream restarts from the same seed; this is uniform across seeds. Diagnosis of the collapsed seed: trajectories begin normally; the deficit concentrates in malformed action envelopes whose parse failures cascade; forgiving every failure with a format tag (the set defined in Section 9) yields 0.7760.776 (Q8_0) and 0.8810.881 (Q3_K_M) for seed 1 (passes 8 and 13, format-only failures 14 and 17, mixed format-and-content failures 30 and 29, all credited), whereas forgiving format-only failures alone yields 22/6722/67 and 30/6730/67. Allowing mixed failures but excluding those with wrong_final_answer yields 0.6870.687 and 0.7460.746. These ceilings associate the collapsed seed with format-tagged failures without establishing that format degrades before reasoning. Under the same forgiveness seeds 2 and 3 reach 0.9100.910 and 0.9550.955 at Q8_0 and 0.8210.821 and 0.9250.925 at Q3_K_M, so the like-for-like comparison places seed 1 inside their band at Q3_K_M and below both at Q8_0; under the stricter forgiveness seeds 2 and 3 reach 0.8810.881 and 0.9250.925 at Q8_0 and 0.8060.806 and 0.8810.881 at Q3_K_M, and seed 1 stays below both bands. The repeated-content hypothesis fails at Q8_0, where seed 3 shows the most repetition (13.7% of steps) and scores 48 of 67; at Q3_K_M the collapsed seed 1 repeats most (9.8% against 2.5% and 3.6%).
